title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Calibration Verification Failure
description: Troubleshoots failed temperature verification caused by setup, simulator condition, probe placement, mode, stabilization, accessories, environment, or internal measurement faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Thermometer From Clinical Use
steps.instructions: Do not use a thermometer that has failed calibration verification or produces results outside the approved verification criteria. Provide another verified thermometer. Label the affected unit to prevent accidental use during evaluation. Expected outcome: No patient temperature is measured with equipment whose accuracy is uncertain.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Verification Method and Failure
steps.instructions: Review the exact test method, equipment used, thermometer mode, displayed reading, expected reading, and acceptance criteria. Use only current approved manufacturer or facility procedures. Do not invent tolerances or use informal comparison methods. Expected outcome: The reported failure is confirmed against the correct documented procedure.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Test Equipment Is Suitable
steps.instructions: Confirm the temperature simulator, calibration device, or verification bath is approved for the thermometer and has current calibration status. Inspect its cable, adapter, well, fluid level, and accessories as applicable. Verify the reference equipment was allowed to warm up or stabilize according to its own instructions. Expected outcome: The test equipment is appropriate, within calibration, and operating normally.

steps.title: 4. Confirm the Correct Probe and Probe Well
steps.instructions: Verify that the correct compatible probe and matching probe well are installed. Inspect the probe tip, cable, connector, and well for contamination, damage, or moisture. Expected outcome: Compatible, intact, clean, and dry external components are being tested.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Correct Measurement Mode
steps.instructions: Confirm that the thermometer is set to the mode required by the approved verification procedure. Do not assume oral, axillary, pediatric, or monitor modes are interchangeable. Expected outcome: The device is tested in the specified mode. If the incorrect mode caused the discrepancy, repeat the verification correctly.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Probe Placement in the Verification Device
steps.instructions: Ensure the probe is inserted to the correct position required by the approved verification setup and remains stable throughout the measurement. Avoid contact with surfaces not intended by the test method. Expected outcome: The sensing area is positioned consistently within the approved test fixture.

steps.title: 7. Allow Adequate Environmental and Equipment Stabilization
steps.instructions: Move the thermometer, probe, and test equipment away from direct airflow, sunlight, heating vents, cold storage, or recent transport between temperature extremes. Allow all components to reach a stable testing environment as required by the approved procedure. Expected outcome: Environmental instability is removed as a source of verification error.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Test Without Changing Multiple Variables
steps.instructions: Repeat the approved verification using the same known-good setup. Record each result rather than relying on memory. If the result passes consistently, investigate whether the original failure was caused by setup or stabilization. Expected outcome: Repeated results are stable and reproducible. A consistent pass allows progression to final functional checks.

steps.title: 9. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: Install a verified compatible probe and repeat the approved verification. Do not adjust internal calibration simply because one probe fails. Expected outcome: The known-good probe passes, identifying the original probe as the cause, or the thermometer still fails and requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Compare With Another Verified Thermometer
steps.instructions: Use the same calibrated verification equipment and method to test another compatible thermometer. This confirms that the verification setup itself can produce an expected result. Expected outcome: The comparison thermometer passes. If both devices fail similarly, stop and investigate the reference setup rather than adjusting either thermometer.

steps.title: 11. Inspect for Intermittent Connections
steps.instructions: During nonpatient verification, observe whether the reading changes or drops out when the probe cable rests in different normal positions. Do not flex the cable aggressively. Expected outcome: The reading remains stable. An intermittent probe, connector, or receptacle requires removal from service.

steps.title: 12. Stop and Escalate a Confirmed Verification Failure
steps.instructions: If the SureTemp Plus 692 fails the approved verification with calibrated test equipment, correct mode, stable conditions, and a known-good probe, do not alter calibration through unauthorized procedures. Expected outcome: The thermometer is removed from service and sent for qualified calibration or repair evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: The SureTemp Plus 692 failed its scheduled temperature accuracy verification.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the probe was not inserted to the required position in the approved verification device, causing unstable readings.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the probe placement and repeated the approved test, with the thermometer passing all required verification checks.

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Configuration, Units, or Default Settings Will Not Save
description: Troubleshoots settings that revert or fail to save due to controls, battery power, workflow, approved configuration, or internal memory faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Prevent Use With Incorrect Settings
steps.instructions: Do not return the thermometer to clinical use when units, measurement mode, or defaults may change unexpectedly. Provide another verified thermometer and clearly identify the affected device. Expected outcome: Staff do not take measurements using uncertain units or configuration.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Setting Does Not Save
steps.instructions: Ask staff which setting was changed, what value was expected, what value returned, and when it reverted. Determine whether the issue follows power-off, battery replacement, probe storage, or a completed measurement. Record the current displayed units and mode before making any changes. Expected outcome: The exact setting and trigger for reversion are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Requested Setting Is Authorized
steps.instructions: Confirm the requested units, defaults, and operating modes match facility policy and the approved device configuration. Do not change protected settings simply to satisfy an individual preference. Expected outcome: The intended configuration is authorized and appropriate for the clinical area.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Normal Setting Procedure
steps.instructions: Use the approved user-level or service-level procedure appropriate to Clinical Engineering. Complete the entire save or exit sequence and allow the thermometer to return to normal operation before powering it off. Do not use undocumented button combinations or unauthorized menus. Expected outcome: The setting is entered and saved using the correct procedure. If it remains after restart, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Keypad and Mode-Button Response
steps.instructions: Confirm every button required for changing and saving the setting responds reliably. Inspect for contamination, sticking, a damaged overlay, or liquid intrusion. Expected outcome: The control sequence is accepted without missed or repeated button presses.

steps.title: 6. Verify Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Install a fresh matched set of correct batteries and inspect the contacts. Weak or interrupted power during configuration may prevent settings from being stored. Expected outcome: The thermometer has stable power throughout configuration and restart.

steps.title: 7. Save One Setting at a Time
steps.instructions: Change only one approved setting, complete the proper save sequence, restart the thermometer, and confirm whether that individual setting remains. This helps identify whether the issue affects all configuration memory or one specific option. Expected outcome: The selected setting remains after restart. If it does, repeat with other authorized settings as needed.

steps.title: 8. Check Whether Battery Removal Causes Reversion
steps.instructions: Record the setting, power the device off normally, restart it, and confirm retention. If appropriate under the approved procedure, then remove and reinstall the batteries and check again. Do not assume all settings are intended to persist through every type of power interruption; verify expected behavior in manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: Setting retention matches documented behavior.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Verified Thermometer
steps.instructions: Compare the configuration process and retention behavior with another SureTemp Plus 692 from the same facility and clinical area. Do not copy settings that are not approved for the affected unit. Expected outcome: The suspect thermometer either behaves normally or is confirmed to have abnormal retention.

steps.title: 10. Confirm Units and Indicators After Measurement
steps.instructions: Using an approved simulator or verification method, complete a measurement and confirm that the displayed units, mode, and default behavior remain correct before, during, and after the cycle. Expected outcome: The approved configuration remains stable through normal operation.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Unauthorized or Unavailable Configuration Changes
steps.instructions: If the requested setting requires a restricted service procedure, configuration tool, or protected access, stop and follow the facility’s authorized escalation process. Expected outcome: Configuration is performed only by qualified personnel using approved documentation.

steps.title: 12. Remove the Device From Service if Settings Revert
steps.instructions: If authorized settings continue to revert despite correct procedure, responsive controls, and fresh batteries, remove the thermometer from service. Expected outcome: A device with unreliable units or defaults is not returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 returned to the previous temperature units after being powered off.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the setting-change sequence had been exited before the save step was completed.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering entered the approved units setting, completed the required save sequence, and verified retention after repeated power cycles and measurements.

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Display Blank, Dim, Missing Segments, or Flickering
description: Troubleshoots unreadable or unstable display conditions caused by batteries, contacts, contamination, viewing conditions, physical damage, or internal display faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove an Unreadable Device From Use
steps.instructions: Do not use the thermometer when temperature values, units, mode indicators, or warning symbols cannot be read reliably. Provide another verified thermometer. Inspect for cracked display windows, liquid intrusion, overheating, odor, battery leakage, or impact damage. Expected outcome: The patient is assessed with a verified alternate device, and the affected thermometer is safely isolated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Display Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the display is completely blank, unusually dim, flickering, missing specific segments, or readable only at certain angles. Ask whether the problem occurs at startup, during measurement, or when the device is moved. Reproduce and document the condition. Expected outcome: The exact display failure and triggering condition are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Remove and inspect the batteries. Replace the full set with fresh, matched, correct batteries and confirm proper polarity. A weak battery set may allow partial startup while causing dimness, flicker, or unstable segments. Expected outcome: The thermometer powers on with stable battery voltage. If the display becomes normal, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Battery Contacts and Compartment
steps.instructions: Check for corrosion, residue, bent contacts, poor spring pressure, loose batteries, or a battery cover that does not secure the cells. Clean only accessible areas using approved procedures and allow the compartment to dry fully. Expected outcome: Battery contact is clean, secure, and stable when the device is handled normally.

steps.title: 5. Check Ambient Lighting and Viewing Angle
steps.instructions: View the display under normal clinical lighting and from the expected operating position. Eliminate glare, direct sunlight, or reflections that may make a functioning display appear dim. Compare readability with another verified SureTemp Plus 692. Expected outcome: The display remains legible in normal use conditions. If the complaint was caused by glare or viewing angle, educate staff and document the finding.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Display Window and Housing
steps.instructions: Clean the external display window using an approved method. Inspect it for scratches, clouding, chemical damage, separation, cracks, or pressure marks. Do not press hard on the display or use abrasive cleaners. Expected outcome: The display window is clean and undamaged, with no external condition obscuring the information.

steps.title: 7. Observe the Complete Startup Display
steps.instructions: Restart the thermometer and observe the display during startup. Note whether all expected segments briefly appear or whether the same areas remain missing. Do not use a thermometer that omits digits or indicators needed to interpret the result safely. Expected outcome: All necessary display segments appear clearly and remain stable. If missing segments persist, remove the device from service.

steps.title: 8. Check for Movement-Related Flicker
steps.instructions: While the device is powered, gently reposition it and observe the display. Do not strike, twist, or flex the housing. If flicker occurs with ordinary handling, suspect an unstable power contact or internal connection. Expected outcome: The display remains stable during normal handling. Any movement-related dropout requires removal from service.

steps.title: 9. Verify Key Indicators During a Functional Measurement
steps.instructions: Use an approved simulator or verification method and confirm that temperature digits, decimal point, units, mode indicators, progress symbols, and alerts remain readable throughout the cycle. Expected outcome: All clinically necessary information remains visible from startup through completed measurement. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate Persistent Display Abnormalities
steps.instructions: If fresh batteries, clean contacts, normal lighting, and an undamaged display window do not correct the problem, do not open the housing or attempt display-board repair. Expected outcome: The thermometer is labeled Out of Service and sent for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 display flickered and became difficult to read during temperature measurements.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found corrosion on one battery contact causing intermittent power to the display.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the accessible battery contact, installed fresh matched batteries, and verified a stable complete display during repeated measurements.

helpfulDetails: Blank, dim, flickering, or missing-segment condition

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Keypad or Mode Button Not Responding
description: Troubleshoots unresponsive controls caused by contamination, stuck buttons, battery instability, operating state, damaged keypad surfaces, or internal control faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Device From Active Use
steps.instructions: Do not attempt to troubleshoot unresponsive controls while the thermometer is being used for patient care. Provide another verified thermometer. If the device cannot be turned off normally, remove the batteries only after the patient is disconnected and the thermometer is out of clinical use. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on a thermometer whose controls cannot be operated reliably.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Controls Are Affected
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether one button, the mode button, or the entire keypad is unresponsive. Determine whether the issue occurs only during a particular screen, measurement stage, or after cleaning. Reproduce the condition and document whether any audible, visual, or display response occurs. Expected outcome: The affected control and operating state are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Thermometer Is in the Correct Operating State
steps.instructions: Return the probe to the well, allow any active measurement cycle to end, and restart the thermometer. Some controls may not respond during certain device states. Do not repeatedly press multiple keys rapidly. Expected outcome: The thermometer reaches its normal ready or standby state and accepts control input. If normal operation returns, perform repeated functional testing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Keypad Surface
steps.instructions: Examine the keypad for dried contamination, adhesive residue, a wrinkled or lifted overlay, cracks, punctures, chemical damage, or signs of liquid intrusion. Clean the surface using an approved method and allow it to dry fully. Do not flood the keypad or use sharp objects. Expected outcome: The keypad is clean, dry, intact, and free of anything that could restrict button movement or contact.

steps.title: 5. Check for a Physically Stuck Button
steps.instructions: Press each external control individually with normal force. Determine whether one button feels continuously depressed, fails to return, or has a different tactile response from the others. Do not pry at the keypad or attempt to lift the overlay. Expected outcome: Each control returns normally after being pressed. A physically damaged or stuck keypad requires removal from service.

steps.title: 6. Verify Battery Condition and Contacts
steps.instructions: Install fresh, matched, correct batteries and inspect the compartment for corrosion, poor contact, or looseness. Unstable power can cause frozen or inconsistent keypad response. Restart the thermometer after battery replacement. Expected outcome: The thermometer powers normally and responds consistently to controls. If battery correction resolves the issue, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Test Each Button Separately
steps.instructions: Operate one button at a time and allow the display to respond. Verify the power control, mode selection, timer or recall functions, and any other available front-panel controls appropriate to the device configuration. Expected outcome: Every required control produces the expected visible response. If all controls operate repeatedly, troubleshooting can stop after measurement verification.

steps.title: 8. Check for Probe or Probe-Well State Conflicts
steps.instructions: Confirm that the probe is recognized and that the probe well correctly detects storage and removal. A storage-detection problem may make the device appear unresponsive because it is not entering the expected control state. Expected outcome: The probe and well state change normally. If correcting the storage condition restores keypad function, complete final testing.

steps.title: 9. Compare Behavior With a Verified Device
steps.instructions: Compare the sequence and response time with another SureTemp Plus 692 configured for the same department. This helps distinguish a normal control limitation from an actual failure. Do not change protected configuration settings simply to make the devices match. Expected outcome: The suspect device responds like the verified comparison unit or is confirmed abnormal.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Complete repeated startup, mode-selection, probe-removal, and approved temperature-verification cycles. Confirm every required button works before, during, and after measurement as intended. Expected outcome: The keypad and mode button respond consistently throughout normal operation. If so, the device may be returned to service.

steps.title: 11. Stop and Escalate an Unresponsive Keypad
steps.instructions: If one or more controls remain unresponsive after cleaning, restarting, checking power, and confirming the correct operating state, remove the thermometer from service. Expected outcome: The device is not returned to use with an intermittent or nonfunctional control interface.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the mode button on the SureTemp Plus 692 did not respond.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried disinfectant residue around the edge of the mode button that restricted normal operation.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and dried the keypad surface and verified repeated mode changes and successful temperature measurements.

helpfulDetails: Whether the problem is constant or intermittent

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Oral, Axillary, or Pediatric Mode Selection Problem
description: Troubleshoots incorrect or unavailable oral, axillary, or pediatric selection caused by probe type, probe well, controls, configuration, or workflow.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Use an Alternate Verified Thermometer
steps.instructions: Do not use the thermometer if the displayed measurement mode does not match the intended patient site or population. Provide another verified thermometer until the correct mode can be reliably selected. Expected outcome: No clinical decision is based on a measurement obtained in an uncertain or incorrect mode.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Mode-Selection Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask staff which mode was intended, which mode appeared, and whether the problem occurs continuously or only after changing probes, wells, batteries, or settings. Reproduce the condition without measuring a patient and document the displayed mode indicators. Expected outcome: The reported mismatch is confirmed and the affected mode is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Installed Probe and Probe Well
steps.instructions: Confirm that the attached probe and installed probe well are the correct compatible type for the intended measurement application. A mismatched probe or probe well may restrict or alter available selections. Inspect both components for modification, damage, or incorrect substitution. Expected outcome: Compatible probe and probe-well components are installed. If correcting a mismatch restores the intended mode, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Probe Is Fully Recognized
steps.instructions: Remove and reinsert the probe while observing the display. Confirm the thermometer recognizes the probe and enters the expected measurement-ready state. If a probe error appears, troubleshoot the probe-recognition issue before evaluating mode selection. Expected outcome: The probe is consistently recognized and no probe error prevents mode selection.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Mode Button and Keypad Area
steps.instructions: Check the mode button and surrounding keypad for contamination, a damaged overlay, sticking, cracks, or evidence of liquid intrusion. Clean the external surface using an approved method and allow it to dry. Do not use sharp tools or excessive force on the keypad. Expected outcome: The button moves or responds normally and is not obstructed by surface contamination.

steps.title: 6. Test Mode Selection Methodically
steps.instructions: With the thermometer in the appropriate ready state, operate the mode control normally and observe each available selection. Allow the display sufficient time to update after each press. Confirm whether the device cycles through the expected options or repeatedly returns to one selection. Expected outcome: The intended oral, axillary, or pediatric selection can be chosen and remains displayed. If so, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 7. Check for User Lockout or Approved Configuration Restrictions
steps.instructions: Review the device’s approved clinical configuration and compare it with another verified SureTemp Plus 692 from the same department. Determine whether a facility-approved setting intentionally limits available modes. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or change protected settings without approved documentation and authorization. Expected outcome: The thermometer’s available modes match the approved configuration. If an authorized configuration correction is required, it is performed by qualified personnel and documented.

steps.title: 8. Verify Battery Condition and Restart the Device
steps.instructions: Low or unstable battery power may contribute to abnormal control behavior. Inspect and replace the batteries with the correct approved type if their condition is uncertain, then restart the thermometer. Preserve approved settings and follow facility procedures when replacing batteries. Expected outcome: The thermometer starts normally and mode selection responds consistently after battery replacement or restart.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good Probe and Probe Well
steps.instructions: Install known-good compatible external components and retest the mode selections. This helps determine whether the issue follows an accessory combination. Expected outcome: The mode selection works with known-good accessories, identifying the original probe or well as the cause, or remains abnormal, indicating a device-side problem.

steps.title: 10. Verify Measurement Behavior in Each Approved Mode
steps.instructions: Using an approved simulator or verification method, confirm that each required mode can be selected, remains active, begins a measurement normally, and produces a stable verified result. Do not use patient measurements as the primary technical test. Expected outcome: Each clinically required mode operates correctly and produces an acceptable verified result. If so, the device may be returned to service.

steps.title: 11. Stop and Escalate Unresolved Mode Problems
steps.instructions: If mode selection remains unavailable, incorrect, or intermittent after checking accessories, the control surface, power, and approved configuration, remove the thermometer from service. Expected outcome: A device that cannot reliably maintain the intended measurement mode is not returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 remained in adult oral mode and would not select the pediatric axillary mode.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the installed probe well did not match the compatible probe and intended measurement application.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering installed the correct compatible probe well and verified normal selection and operation of the required measurement modes.

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Persistent Error Code After Probe Replacement
description: Troubleshoots a continuing error after probe replacement caused by incompatibility, connection, probe well, contamination, power, configuration, or device-side faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Thermometer From Use
steps.instructions: Do not use the thermometer while an unresolved error remains, even if a new probe has been installed. Provide another verified device for patient temperature measurement. Document the exact displayed code or message without interpreting it beyond available manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely, and the original error information is preserved.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Replacement History
steps.instructions: Determine why the probe was replaced, whether the original and replacement probes produced the same error, and whether the error began before or after replacement. Record the replacement probe’s source, compatibility, and condition. Expected outcome: The sequence of events is clear and unnecessary repeated probe replacement is avoided.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Replacement Probe Is Compatible
steps.instructions: Confirm that the replacement probe is approved for the SureTemp Plus 692 and matches the installed probe well and intended measurement application. Inspect for packaging damage, an incorrect connector, or a probe intended for another model. Expected outcome: A correct compatible replacement probe is installed. If the probe is incompatible, install the proper accessory and retest.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the New Probe Before Use
steps.instructions: Even a new probe may be damaged. Inspect the probe, cable, strain relief, connector, and tip for cracks, bent contacts, contamination, pinched packaging damage, or moisture. Expected outcome: The replacement probe is visibly intact and dry.

steps.title: 5. Inspect and Reseat the Probe Connector
steps.instructions: Power the thermometer off. Disconnect the probe and inspect both the plug and thermometer receptacle for debris, corrosion, moisture, damaged alignment features, or bent contacts. Reconnect the probe securely and restart the thermometer. Expected outcome: The probe is fully seated and the error clears. If so, perform repeated functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Probe Well
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct probe well is installed, fully seated, clean, and undamaged. Remove accessible debris and replace a cracked or warped well. A storage-detection or probe-well problem may remain even after the probe itself is replaced. Expected outcome: Probe-well detection is normal and no storage fault contributes to the error.

steps.title: 7. Install Fresh Verified Batteries
steps.instructions: Replace the complete battery set with fresh, matched, correct batteries and inspect the contacts. Restart the device using only the standard operating procedure. Unstable power can preserve or retrigger an error condition. Expected outcome: The thermometer starts normally with stable power. If the error clears, complete repeated measurements and verification.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Second Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: When available, test with a probe that is already verified on another compatible thermometer. This prevents a defective replacement probe from misleading the diagnosis. Expected outcome: The known-good probe either clears the error, identifying the replacement probe as faulty, or produces the same error, indicating a device-side or probe-well issue.

steps.title: 9. Test the Replacement Probe on Another Compatible Device
steps.instructions: Connect the replacement probe to a verified compatible SureTemp Plus 692 when safe and practical. Follow infection-control precautions and do not use the comparison device for patient care during testing. Expected outcome: The replacement probe functions normally on the comparison device or reproduces the error and is removed from use.

steps.title: 10. Check Approved Configuration and Normal Startup State
steps.instructions: Compare the suspect thermometer with another department unit using the same approved configuration. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or clear diagnostic history through undocumented procedures. Expected outcome: No approved setting or accessory mismatch is contributing to the persistent error.

steps.title: 11. Perform Approved Functional and Accuracy Testing
steps.instructions: If the error clears, complete repeated probe insertion, removal, mode selection, measurement, and temperature-verification testing using approved equipment. Expected outcome: The error does not recur and the thermometer completes stable, accurate measurements. If the error returns, remove the device from service.

steps.title: 12. Stop Replacing External Parts and Escalate
steps.instructions: If two known-good compatible probes, a verified probe well, secure connections, and fresh batteries do not clear the error, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The thermometer is labeled Out of Service and routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 continued to display the same probe-related error after a new probe was installed.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found debris inside the external probe receptacle that prevented the replacement probe from seating completely.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and dried the accessible receptacle, securely connected the replacement probe, and verified repeated error-free measurements and temperature accuracy.

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Probe Heater or Predictive Measurement Failure
description: Troubleshoots predictive measurement or probe-conditioning problems caused by accessories, probe state, mode, contamination, environment, batteries, or internal faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Use Another Verified Thermometer
steps.instructions: Do not use the thermometer for patient assessment when predictive measurement fails, the probe does not condition normally, or results are delayed or unstable. Provide another verified thermometer. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on an uncertain predictive measurement system.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether the device displays an error, fails to enter predictive mode, remains in an alternate measurement state, takes unusually long, or produces inconsistent readings. Document the probe type, selected mode, measurement site, and displayed indicators. Expected outcome: The reported predictive or probe-conditioning failure is reproduced and defined.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Probe and Probe Well
steps.instructions: Confirm that the installed probe and probe well are compatible with the SureTemp Plus 692 and the intended measurement application. Inspect for mismatched colors, incorrect accessories, or substituted components. Expected outcome: The correct accessory combination is installed. If correcting the mismatch restores predictive operation, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Probe Recognition and Storage Detection
steps.instructions: Insert the probe fully into the well and confirm normal storage detection. Remove it and verify that the thermometer enters the expected ready state without a probe error. A storage-detection fault may prevent proper probe preparation or predictive operation. Expected outcome: Probe storage and removal are recognized consistently.

steps.title: 5. Inspect and Clean the Probe
steps.instructions: Inspect the probe tip, cable, body, connector, and strain relief for contamination, moisture, cracks, or damage. Clean and dry external surfaces using approved procedures. Do not apply direct heat to the probe or immerse it unless specifically allowed. Expected outcome: The probe is clean, dry, intact, and securely connected.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Proper Probe-Cover Installation
steps.instructions: Install one correct compatible probe cover and verify it is fully seated. Check for doubled, loose, wrinkled, damaged, or contaminated covers. Expected outcome: The probe cover fits correctly and does not interfere with temperature sensing.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Intended Measurement Mode
steps.instructions: Confirm that the selected mode matches the measurement site and patient population. A different mode may use a different measurement behavior and be mistaken for predictive failure. Expected outcome: The intended predictive mode is selected and remains displayed.

steps.title: 8. Allow the Probe and Device to Stabilize
steps.instructions: If the thermometer was moved from a hot, cold, or high-airflow environment, allow it to stabilize in normal room conditions. Keep it away from direct sunlight, heating vents, and cold exterior walls. Expected outcome: Environmental temperature does not interfere with probe conditioning or predictive calculations.

steps.title: 9. Verify Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Install fresh, matched, correct batteries and inspect the contacts. Unstable power can affect measurement processing and probe-related operation. Expected outcome: The thermometer has stable power and no low-battery indication.

steps.title: 10. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: Install a verified compatible probe and repeat the test with an approved simulator or manufacturer-authorized verification setup. Expected outcome: Predictive measurement operates normally with the known-good probe, identifying the original probe as defective, or the failure remains and indicates a device-side problem.

steps.title: 11. Perform Repeated Approved Functional Measurements
steps.instructions: Complete several controlled measurements and confirm the device enters the expected mode, progresses normally, completes the cycle, and produces stable verified results. Do not touch the probe tip to judge whether a heater is operating, and do not apply external heat as a diagnostic method. Expected outcome: Predictive measurement completes consistently and passes approved verification. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 12. Stop and Escalate Confirmed Predictive Failure
steps.instructions: If the failure remains with known-good accessories, fresh batteries, correct mode, proper probe storage, and stable environmental conditions, remove the thermometer from service. Expected outcome: The thermometer is routed for qualified internal evaluation rather than returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 would not complete predictive temperature measurements.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the probe was not seating fully in the probe well because the well was obstructed by dried residue.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the probe well, confirmed normal probe storage detection, and verified repeated predictive measurements with acceptable temperature results.

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Probe Not Recognized or Probe Error
description: Troubleshoots an unrecognized temperature probe, probe-related error, damaged connection, incompatible probe, contamination, or external accessory failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Temperature-Monitoring Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not continue using the thermometer for clinical decisions when the probe is not recognized or the displayed temperature cannot be trusted. Remove it from patient use and provide staff with another verified thermometer. Inspect for liquid intrusion, cracked housings, exposed conductors, overheating, unusual odor, or other visible damage. Remove the device from service immediately if any unsafe condition is present. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with a verified alternate thermometer, and the affected device is safe to evaluate.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff when the problem occurs and document any displayed message or symbol. Determine whether the probe is never recognized, becomes recognized intermittently, or produces an error only when removed from the probe well. Power the thermometer on and reproduce the condition without using it on a patient. Expected outcome: The exact probe-recognition symptom is confirmed under controlled conditions. If the device now recognizes the probe consistently, complete functional verification before returning it to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Probe Type and Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm that the attached probe is intended for the SureTemp Plus 692 and is appropriate for the installed probe well and measurement application. Inspect for incorrect, substituted, or visibly modified accessories. Do not force an incompatible connector into the thermometer. Expected outcome: The correct compatible probe and probe well are installed. If replacing an incorrect accessory restores recognition, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Probe and Cable
steps.instructions: Examine the entire probe cable for cuts, crushing, severe kinks, stretched sections, discoloration, exposed conductors, or damage near strain-relief points. Inspect the probe tip and body for cracks, contamination, bent components, or evidence of liquid intrusion. Clean external surfaces according to approved infection-control and manufacturer guidance. Do not immerse components unless specifically permitted. Expected outcome: The probe and cable are clean, intact, and free of visible damage. A damaged probe must be replaced before further testing.

steps.title: 5. Inspect and Reseat the Probe Connection
steps.instructions: Power the thermometer off. Disconnect the probe using the correct release method, then inspect the plug and device receptacle for debris, moisture, corrosion, bent contacts, pushed-back contacts, or damaged plastic alignment features. Allow any approved cleaning agent to dry fully. Reconnect the probe firmly without excessive force, then restart the thermometer. Expected outcome: The connection is fully seated and the probe is recognized. If normal operation returns and remains stable, proceed to final functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Check the Probe Well and Storage Position
steps.instructions: Verify that the correct probe well is fully installed and not cracked, loose, contaminated, or obstructed. Confirm that the probe can be inserted and removed normally without binding. A probe well or storage fault may affect how the thermometer detects probe removal and initiates measurement. Expected outcome: The correct probe well is secure, unobstructed, and properly detects probe storage and removal. If correcting the well resolves the error, troubleshooting can stop after final testing.

steps.title: 7. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible probe that has been verified on another SureTemp Plus 692, when available. Avoid using a probe with an uncertain history. Observe whether the thermometer recognizes the known-good probe through several insertion and removal cycles. Expected outcome: The known-good probe is recognized consistently. If it works normally, replace the original probe and complete functional verification.

steps.title: 8. Compare the Suspect Probe on Another Compatible Thermometer
steps.instructions: When safe and practical, connect the suspect probe to another verified compatible SureTemp Plus 692. Use infection-control precautions and do not cross-contaminate accessories. This comparison helps separate a probe failure from a thermometer-side connection or detection problem. Expected outcome: The suspect probe either fails on the second device, confirming an accessory problem, or works normally, indicating the original thermometer requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Functional Check
steps.instructions: With the recognized probe installed, verify that removing the probe from the well initiates the expected measurement-ready condition. Confirm that the device completes a nonpatient functional measurement using an approved temperature simulator or manufacturer-authorized verification method. Do not use informal comparisons against room temperature, hands, or unverified household thermometers as a calibration determination. Expected outcome: The probe is recognized, the measurement cycle begins normally, and the device produces a stable result using approved verification equipment.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate When Recognition Remains Unreliable
steps.instructions: If the error remains after checking compatibility, condition, cleanliness, seating, the probe well, and a known-good probe, do not continue swapping accessories indefinitely or open the device for board-level troubleshooting. Expected outcome: An unresolved or intermittent thermometer is removed from service and routed for qualified bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 displayed a probe error and would not begin a temperature measurement.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the probe connector was not fully seated and contained dried surface contamination around the connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and dried the external connection, reseated the probe, and verified consistent probe recognition and successful temperature verification testing.

helpfulDetails: Exact probe error message or symbol
Condition of the connector and receptacle
Whether the issue was constant or intermittent

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Probe Well Not Detected or Probe Storage Fault
description: Troubleshoots failure to detect the probe well or stored probe due to installation, contamination, damage, obstruction, or sensing problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a probe-storage detection problem while the thermometer is being relied upon for patient assessment. Remove it from clinical use and provide another verified thermometer. Inspect the thermometer, probe well, probe, and cable for cracks, liquid intrusion, exposed conductors, or other unsafe conditions. Expected outcome: Patient temperature monitoring continues with a verified alternative, and the affected thermometer is safe to inspect.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Storage Fault
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether the thermometer fails to recognize that the probe is stored, fails to enter the expected mode when the probe is removed, or displays an error continuously. Document any message, symbol, or unusual behavior. Reproduce the problem by carefully inserting and removing the probe several times. Expected outcome: The exact failure point is identified. If the condition cannot be reproduced, inspect for intermittent fit or obstruction and complete repeated functional checks.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Probe Well Is Installed
steps.instructions: Confirm that the installed probe well is compatible with the attached probe and intended measurement application. Check for a mismatched, substituted, or improperly fitted well. Do not modify or force the probe well into place. Expected outcome: The correct probe well is installed. If installing the correct component restores normal detection, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Remove and Inspect the Probe Well
steps.instructions: Power the thermometer off. Remove the probe well using the normal external removal method. Inspect it for cracks, warping, broken retaining features, contamination, foreign material, or an object lodged inside. Clean or replace the probe well according to approved procedures. Allow it to dry completely before reinstallation. Expected outcome: The probe well is clean, dry, undamaged, and free of obstruction.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Probe-Well Mounting Area
steps.instructions: Examine the accessible mounting area for debris, dried cleaning solution, damaged plastic, misalignment, or other conditions that prevent full seating. Do not insert metal tools or probe internal switches or contacts. Remove only accessible external debris using approved cleaning methods. Expected outcome: The mounting area is clean and unobstructed, allowing the well to seat fully.

steps.title: 6. Reinstall the Probe Well Correctly
steps.instructions: Reinstall the well in the proper orientation and confirm it is fully seated and stable. It should not remain loose, rock excessively, or sit partially raised. Restart the thermometer and observe whether the storage fault clears. Expected outcome: The thermometer detects the installed probe well. If normal detection returns, proceed to repeated insertion and removal testing.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Probe Fit Within the Well
steps.instructions: Insert the probe and verify that it reaches its normal stored position without excessive resistance. Check whether the cable or strain relief prevents complete insertion. Inspect the probe body for cracks, deformation, or contamination that could interfere with proper storage. Expected outcome: The probe seats fully and remains securely stored. If cleaning or replacing a damaged probe restores proper detection, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Probe Well
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible probe well, when available. Repeat several probe insertion and removal cycles while observing device behavior. Expected outcome: The known-good well is detected consistently. If it resolves the fault, replace the original well and document the accessory failure.

steps.title: 9. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: If the fault remains, test with a verified compatible probe. A damaged or misshapen probe body may prevent proper storage detection even when the well is functional. Expected outcome: The known-good probe stores and removes normally. If it works, replace the original probe and complete final verification.

steps.title: 10. Verify Normal Measurement-State Transitions
steps.instructions: With the probe stored, confirm the thermometer remains in its expected standby state. Remove the probe and verify that the device enters the appropriate measurement-ready condition. Return the probe to the well and confirm the cycle resets normally. Expected outcome: The thermometer consistently detects stored and removed positions over multiple cycles. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 11. Escalate an Unresolved Detection Problem
steps.instructions: If the fault remains with known-good compatible external components, do not disassemble the housing or attempt to bypass the storage-detection mechanism. Expected outcome: The thermometer is removed from service and referred for service-level evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 did not recognize when the probe was placed in or removed from the probe well.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the probe well was partially unseated because dried residue was present in the mounting area.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the accessible mounting area, reinstalled the probe well, and verified normal storage detection and repeated measurement initiation.

helpfulDetails: Presence of debris or cleaning residue
Whether the well was fully seated
Number of successful insertion and removal cycles

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Rapid Battery Drain or Low Battery Warning Persists
description: Troubleshoots short battery life or persistent low-battery indication caused by batteries, contacts, installation, contamination, storage, or abnormal power consumption.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain an Available Backup
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a thermometer that may shut down during patient assessment. Provide another verified thermometer and remove the affected device from active clinical use during evaluation. Inspect for heat, odor, swollen batteries, corrosion, leakage, or liquid intrusion. Use appropriate precautions when handling damaged batteries. Expected outcome: Patient care is uninterrupted, and unsafe batteries or equipment are isolated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Battery Problem
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether batteries drain during use, while stored, or immediately after replacement. Determine whether the low-battery indication appears continuously, intermittently, or only during measurement. Document battery brand, type, age, installation date, and estimated usage when known. Expected outcome: The battery complaint is defined well enough to distinguish actual drain from an incorrect warning indication.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Battery Type and Complete Set
steps.instructions: Confirm that all installed batteries are the approved size and chemistry specified for the thermometer. Do not mix old and new batteries, brands, chemistries, or cells with different charge states. Replace the complete set with fresh, matched batteries from a reliable supply. Expected outcome: A matched set of correct batteries is installed. If the warning clears and runtime is normal, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Battery Orientation and Compartment Closure
steps.instructions: Inspect the polarity markings and confirm every battery is installed in the correct direction. Ensure the battery compartment cover is fully closed and secure. A partially installed battery or loose cover may create intermittent power and false low-battery indications. Expected outcome: All batteries are correctly oriented and held securely.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Battery Compartment
steps.instructions: Remove the batteries and inspect accessible contacts and the compartment for corrosion, residue, bent contacts, weakened spring tension, contamination, or signs of prior battery leakage. Clean only according to approved procedures. Do not scrape contacts aggressively or apply unapproved chemicals. Expected outcome: Contacts are clean, dry, intact, and provide firm pressure against the batteries.

steps.title: 6. Check the Replacement Batteries Independently
steps.instructions: Use an appropriate battery tester or digital multimeter to compare the fresh cells before and after installation. Identify a weak or defective cell within the set. Do not judge battery condition only by package age or appearance. Expected outcome: Each installed battery is in comparable, serviceable condition. A weak cell is replaced as part of a complete matched set.

steps.title: 7. Observe Startup and Low-Battery Indication
steps.instructions: Start the thermometer several times and observe whether the low-battery symbol appears immediately, only under measurement load, or after a period of operation. Gently reposition the device without striking or shaking it and watch for power interruptions that may indicate poor contact. Expected outcome: The thermometer starts consistently and the warning remains cleared with fresh batteries. If the warning persists immediately, further evaluation is required.

steps.title: 8. Check for Controls or Mechanical Conditions Keeping the Device Active
steps.instructions: Inspect the keypad and probe-storage area for stuck buttons, a probe that does not seat correctly, or a storage-detection fault that may prevent normal standby behavior. Verify the thermometer transitions to its expected idle state after the probe is returned to the well. Expected outcome: No stuck control or storage fault keeps the device unnecessarily active.

steps.title: 9. Compare Runtime Under Controlled Conditions
steps.instructions: Install fresh verified batteries, record the date, and perform repeated nonpatient functional cycles over a controlled observation period. Compare behavior with another verified SureTemp Plus 692 under similar use when practical. Avoid declaring excessive drain based on an unknown prior battery history. Expected outcome: Battery indication and operating time remain stable during controlled use. If the fresh batteries decline abnormally, remove the device from service.

steps.title: 10. Verify the Warning Clears After Battery Replacement
steps.instructions: After installing known-good batteries, restart the thermometer and confirm that the low-battery warning clears. If the display retains an old indication, perform only the manufacturer-supported normal restart procedure. Do not enter unauthorized service modes or alter internal calibration data. Expected outcome: The warning accurately reflects the condition of the installed batteries.

steps.title: 11. Stop and Escalate Persistent Battery Drain
steps.instructions: If known-good matched batteries drain rapidly or the low-battery warning remains despite clean, intact contacts, do not continue clinical use. Expected outcome: The thermometer is labeled and routed for internal power-management or display-circuit evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 continued to show a low-battery warning immediately after battery replacement.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found mixed battery brands and one weak cell installed in the battery compartment.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering installed a complete matched set of verified batteries and confirmed the warning cleared through repeated startup and measurement testing.

helpfulDetails: Presence of stuck keys or storage faults

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Reading Cycle Takes Too Long or Never Completes
description: Troubleshoots delayed or incomplete temperature cycles caused by technique, probe covers, positioning, mode, movement, probe condition, environment, or device faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Avoid Delayed Clinical Assessment
steps.instructions: Do not repeatedly attempt a prolonged measurement when the patient’s condition requires timely assessment. Provide another verified thermometer and remove the affected unit from use during troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient care is not delayed by an unreliable temperature cycle.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Cycle Behavior
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether the measurement starts slowly, remains active indefinitely, restarts, changes modes, or ends without a result. Determine the measurement site, patient population, probe type, and whether a probe cover was used. Reproduce the condition using an approved nonpatient test method. Expected outcome: The delay is confirmed and associated conditions are documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify Probe Recognition and Ready State
steps.instructions: Confirm that removing the probe from the well places the thermometer in the expected ready condition. Resolve any probe or probe-well detection error first. Expected outcome: The thermometer recognizes the probe and begins a measurement cycle normally.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Probe and Cable
steps.instructions: Check the probe tip, cable, connector, and strain relief for contamination, cracks, moisture, severe bends, or intermittent damage. Clean and dry external surfaces according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: The probe is clean, dry, intact, and securely connected.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Correct Probe Cover
steps.instructions: Confirm that the probe cover is compatible, fully seated, undamaged, and used only once. Check for doubled covers, loose covers, wrinkles, trapped debris, or an incorrectly installed cover. Do not test patients without required infection-control barriers. Expected outcome: A single correct probe cover is installed securely. If correcting the cover restores normal cycle completion, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Confirm the Intended Measurement Mode
steps.instructions: Verify that the selected oral, axillary, pediatric, or other approved mode matches the intended measurement site and patient population. Incorrect mode selection may alter measurement behavior. Expected outcome: The correct mode is displayed and remains selected.

steps.title: 7. Review Positioning and Measurement Technique
steps.instructions: For clinical observations, verify that staff are placing the probe at the intended anatomical site and maintaining stable contact according to approved practice. Identify movement, talking, poor tissue contact, recent eating or drinking, or other factors that may prevent prediction from stabilizing. Clinical Engineering should not use a patient as the primary technical test. Expected outcome: Technique-related causes are identified and corrected through staff education when appropriate.

steps.title: 8. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Move the thermometer away from direct airflow, temperature extremes, sunlight, or recent transition from a hot or cold storage area. Allow the device and probe to stabilize in the clinical environment. Expected outcome: Environmental conditions no longer interfere with measurement stabilization.

steps.title: 9. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: Install a verified compatible probe and repeat the cycle using an approved simulator or functional verification method. Expected outcome: The known-good probe completes the cycle normally, identifying the original probe as defective, or the delay remains and points toward a device-side problem.

steps.title: 10. Verify Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Install fresh, matched, correct batteries and inspect the contacts. Low or unstable power can cause slow processing, restarts, or incomplete cycles. Expected outcome: The thermometer operates with stable power. If fresh batteries correct the delay, complete repeated measurements.

steps.title: 11. Perform Repeated Controlled Measurements
steps.instructions: Complete several measurements with the same approved test setup, allowing the device to reset normally between cycles. Record whether completion time and results are consistent. Do not invent a maximum cycle duration; compare behavior with approved documentation or a verified comparison unit. Expected outcome: Measurements complete consistently and produce stable verified readings. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 12. Stop and Escalate an Incomplete Cycle
steps.instructions: If the cycle remains excessively prolonged or never completes with a known-good probe, correct mode, stable environment, proper test setup, and fresh batteries, remove the thermometer from service. Expected outcome: The unreliable thermometer is prevented from delaying or compromising patient care.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 remained in the measurement cycle and did not produce a temperature.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the probe cover was not fully seated and was wrinkled around the probe tip.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering installed a new compatible probe cover correctly and verified repeated completed measurements with stable temperature results.

helpfulDetails: Whether the cycle starts, stalls, or restarts

title: Welch Allyn SureTemp Plus 692 Thermometer - Temperature Reading Intermittently Drops Out
description: Troubleshoots intermittent temperature loss caused by probe movement, damaged cables, loose connections, batteries, probe covers, contacts, or device-side faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Unreliable Thermometer From Use
steps.instructions: Do not continue using a thermometer whose reading disappears, resets, freezes, or becomes unavailable during measurement. Provide another verified thermometer. If dropout occurs during a clinical assessment, disregard the incomplete result. Expected outcome: The patient is assessed with a reliable device, and the intermittent thermometer is isolated for testing.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Dropout Pattern
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether the display blanks, the temperature digits disappear, the measurement restarts, a probe error appears, or the entire device powers off. Determine whether the problem occurs when the probe, cable, thermometer, or patient moves. Reproduce the condition without using it on a patient. Expected outcome: The dropout is associated with a specific type of movement, stage, or displayed symptom.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Probe and Cable Closely
steps.instructions: Examine the cable from the probe tip to the connector. Look for cuts, crushing, severe bends, stretched sections, discoloration, exposed conductors, or damage near either strain relief. Do not aggressively flex a suspect cable. Expected outcome: The cable is intact. Any visible damage requires probe replacement.

steps.title: 4. Inspect and Reseat the Probe Connector
steps.instructions: Power the thermometer off. Disconnect the probe and inspect the connector and device receptacle for debris, moisture, corrosion, bent contacts, damaged alignment features, or looseness. Clean and dry accessible areas using approved procedures, then reconnect the probe fully. Expected outcome: The connection is secure and the reading remains stable. If reseating resolves the dropout, proceed to repeated testing.

steps.title: 5. Verify Probe-Well Detection
steps.instructions: Insert and remove the probe several times. Confirm that the thermometer consistently detects the stored and measurement-ready states. An intermittent storage-detection fault may interrupt or reset the measurement sequence. Expected outcome: Probe-well state changes are detected consistently.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Probe Cover
steps.instructions: Confirm that a single compatible probe cover is installed securely and does not loosen during the cycle. Replace wrinkled, damaged, contaminated, or poorly fitting covers. Expected outcome: The probe cover remains stable and does not interrupt tissue contact or sensing.

steps.title: 7. Verify Battery Condition and Contacts
steps.instructions: Install fresh, matched, correct batteries. Inspect the compartment for corrosion, weak contact pressure, residue, or a loose cover. Observe whether the entire device resets when gently repositioned. Expected outcome: Power remains stable during normal handling and measurement.

steps.title: 8. Test the Probe Cable in Normal Positions
steps.instructions: Using an approved nonpatient test setup, allow the cable to rest in several normal positions while observing the reading. Move the cable slowly near each strain relief without excessive bending. Stop immediately if dropout is reproduced. Expected outcome: The reading remains stable. If dropout follows cable position, replace the probe.

steps.title: 9. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: Install a verified compatible probe and repeat the controlled measurement and normal-position testing. Expected outcome: The known-good probe remains stable, confirming the original probe or cable caused the dropout, or the problem remains and points toward the thermometer.

steps.title: 10. Compare the Suspect Probe on Another Compatible Thermometer
steps.instructions: When appropriate, connect the suspect probe to another verified SureTemp Plus 692 and repeat the controlled test. Follow infection-control procedures and do not use the comparison unit clinically during testing. Expected outcome: The dropout follows the suspect probe or remains isolated to the original thermometer.

steps.title: 11. Check Display Stability Independently
steps.instructions: Observe whether other display indicators flicker or disappear when the temperature drops out. A full display interruption may indicate a power or display problem rather than loss of temperature sensing alone. Expected outcome: The dropout is classified as a probe-signal interruption, measurement reset, or complete power/display interruption.

steps.title: 12. Perform Repeated Functional and Accuracy Verification
steps.instructions: Complete several approved temperature-verification cycles with the corrected or known-good components. Confirm the reading remains visible and stable throughout each cycle and that results meet approved criteria. Expected outcome: No dropout occurs during repeated testing and temperature verification passes. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 13. Stop and Escalate an Intermittent Device-Side Fault
steps.instructions: If the reading still drops out with a known-good probe, secure connection, fresh batteries, and stable test setup, remove the thermometer from service. Expected outcome: The intermittent device is not returned to clinical use without qualified repair and verification.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SureTemp Plus 692 temperature reading disappeared whenever the probe cable was moved.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering reproduced the dropout and found an intermittent cable near the probe strain relief.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the probe and verified stable readings through repeated cable-position tests and approved temperature verification.
